solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rough tune heard from this pirate

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: rough means coarse and a tune is an air

explanation.surface: A gruff melody drifts from a buccaneer's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a privateer or sea raider, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Copper provoking excitement in church office

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
racy means lively or titillating

explanation.surface: A policeman causes a stir in a parish post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the post held by a curate, an assistant clergyman.

clue.text: Note sexy woman's makeover

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a vamp is a seductive woman; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A memo about a seductress getting a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: A revamp is a renovation or overhaul, giving something a fresh appearance.

clue.text: Officially approved writer is top man on paper

parts.note: an author is a writer
the editor is the head of a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: An authorised author is the boss at a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorised means sanctioned or given official permission.

clue.text: Preacher to prattle endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for prattle loses its final letter

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chatter at length

explanation.surface: A preacher who goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit on' is British slang for talking at tedious length.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher who preaches to a congregation.

clue.text: Entertaining a thought

parts.note: a musing is a reflection or thought

explanation.surface: Contemplating an idea for one's guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining a thought' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing means diverting or funny, which is what entertaining things are.

clue.text: Ace off to Saturn?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are spoiled or set in disorder

explanation.surface: A star pilot sets out for the ringed planet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is also the definition: a crack pilot heading off towards a distant planet is exactly the kind of person meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a space traveller, who might be an ace flying off to another planet.

clue.text: State when taking dust-bath regularly

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird enjoying a dust-bath somewhere in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Hear Isis is choppy body of water

indicators.note: choppy water is rough and broken up, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: Listen: the Isis is rough today.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name for the Thames at Oxford, a nice watery distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Sea is the stretch of sea between Ireland and Great Britain.

clue.text: Worker with small arms finds Cambridge college hard after comfortable upbringing

indicators.note: after puts the college and hard behind the reversed word
in a down clue upbringing means bringing up, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: snug means cosy and comfortable
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A craftsman finds a Cambridge place tough after a cosy childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge college' tempts towards Cambridge, England; it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. 'upbringing' turns SNUG into GUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunsmith makes and repairs firearms, including small arms.

clue.text: Right one to scrutinise one joining

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to vet is to examine carefully

explanation.surface: The proper person to examine a new member.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin used to fasten plates together.

clue.text: Many soldiers strike irregular force, one showing courage

parts.note: to bat is to hit
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve
a lion is a brave person

explanation.surface: A ragtag militia's hero hits back hard.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve, here 'irregular' as not regular army.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large army unit of several companies.

clue.text: Batty admirer, would-be lover, non-U type is set up by him

definitions.text: type is set up by him

parts.note: Compo, in the BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, forever pursued Nora Batty

indicators.note: non-U says the letter U is to be taken out of the lover word

parts.note: a suitor courts someone hoping to win them

explanation.surface: An eccentric fan and an unrefined wooer get set up for a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like 'crazy' but is Nora Batty of the BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, whose admirer was Compo. 'Non-U' (not upper-class) drops U.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor is a printer's worker who sets type by hand or machine.

clue.text: Football team shortly to make a great strike

indicators.note: shortly says the club name is cut down

parts.note: West Ham United is a London football club

explanation.surface: A football club soon scores a stunning goal.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is a London football club; cut short it becomes W HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To wham is to hit something with a heavy forceful blow.

clue.text: Starts to bash excellent tennis stroke in anticipation

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the forehand is a basic tennis shot

explanation.surface: A tennis player prepares to bash a fine forehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand means in advance, ahead of time.

clue.text: False account from distinguished politicians leaving south in a haze

indicators.note: in places the politicians inside the haze

parts.note: mist is a haze

indicators.note: leaving says one letter departs from the politicians

parts.note: statesmen are respected political leaders

explanation.surface: Great politicians, confused and minus the South, give a misleading report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes only one of the two S's from the politicians, so the second S of the answer comes from elsewhere in the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstatement is an incorrect or misleading statement.

clue.text: Sentence for minor offence may be this — hanging

definitions.text: Sentence for minor offence may be this
definitions.meaning: a ... sentence is not served unless the offender reoffends

explanation.definitionFit: Suspended describes both a deferred prison term and something hanging in the air.

clue.text: In poor condition for record, withdraw from race? Yes

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw an entrant from a race

explanation.surface: A runner pulls out of the race, then says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratchy vinyl disc crackles from surface damage.

clue.text: Shelter mare with bull? — that's irregular

indicators.note: irregular says the letters are not in their usual order

explanation.surface: Housing a mare with a bull is unusual farming.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella gives shelter from rain, and figuratively any protective cover.

clue.text: Reorganising cannot impose to make amends

indicators.note: reorganising says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restructure cannot be forced to make up for losses.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation is recompense or redress, making good a loss.

clue.text: Museum finally foil one causing damage

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: finally says take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A museum thwarts a destroyer at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal deliberately destroys or damages property.

clue.text: A drop of rum in ale or porter perhaps

indicators.note: in puts A and the drop inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: a drop of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Spiking a pint with rum gives you a dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like the dark beer, fitting the surface, but it is a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter carries loads, so is one example of a bearer.

clue.text: Some land endlessly set aside for religious use

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses both its ends

parts.note: sacred means consecrated or dedicated to religion

explanation.surface: A plot reserved for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area.

clue.text: Intended to return to prison, apparently

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the reverse of setting free

explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate means intentional; jokingly, de-liberating someone would be undoing their release.

clue.text: Clumsy writer got up in it

indicators.note: in puts the reversed writer inside it
in a down clue got up means written upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An awkward writer got up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means unskilled or clumsy.

clue.text: This dish will make you flourish

definitions.text: This dish will make you flourish

parts.words: This dish will make you flourish
parts.note: a breakfast cereal said to keep you healthy; put this before dish and it spells a word meaning to wave about

explanation.definitionFit: Bran is a cereal food, and with dish after it forms a word for waving a weapon.

clue.text: Poet made clear in heartless academy

indicators.note: in places the cleared word inside the institution
heartless removes the middle letter

parts.note: a college is an academy
rid means cleared or freed

explanation.surface: A poet clarifies things in a soulless school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made clear' is past tense: to rid is to clear, and the past tense is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Snake, I reckon

definitions.meaning: one who reckons figures, a person who adds

explanation.definitionFit: An adder is a viper, and also someone who adds up or reckons.

clue.text: Had strong urge to repair deanery

indicators.note: repair suggests putting the letters back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Longed to fix up the dean's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearned means longed for something intensely.

clue.text: Tumbler has some of its contents replaced by rum tot

indicators.text: has some of its contents replaced by
indicators.note: says part of the inside of the glass word is swapped out

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: A glass has some of its rum swapped for a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbler' and 'tot' both look like drinks or glasses; tot is a small child, and a tumbler is one who falls over a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, as is a toddler.
